tc-gauche-1.explanation: The sentence grades one social offence as worse than another, so the blank is a stronger word for tactlessness, which gauche supplies; urbane and decorous say the opposite.
tc-gauche-1.stem: Praising the catering at a funeral is merely clumsy; asking the widow what the house is now worth is _____ in a way that no apology quite repairs.

tc-hegemony-1.explanation: One studio deciding what the public can see is dominance over the others, which hegemony names; autonomy and parity describe independence and equality instead.
tc-hegemony-1.stem: For half a century one studio's _____ over distribution meant that a film it declined to carry effectively did not exist outside the city it was shot in.

tc-impugn-1.explanation: Attacking the accountant instead of the figures means casting doubt on him, which impugn says; corroborate, exonerate and vindicate would all support him.
tc-impugn-1.stem: Rather than answer the audit line by line, the chairman chose to _____ the motives of the accountant who had ordered it in the first place.

tc-ingratiate-1.explanation: Birthdays, flowers and reflexive agreement are calculated to win the trustees over, which is what ingratiate means; the other four would drive them away.
tc-ingratiate-1.stem: Every gesture of that first month was designed to _____ him with the trustees: remembered birthdays, agreement with whoever had spoken last, flowers after each meeting.

tc-invective-1.explanation: The letter degenerates from reasoned complaint into an attack on people, which is invective; panegyric is praise and the others describe faulty or evasive wording.
tc-invective-1.stem: The first page is a reasoned complaint about the schedule; by the third the letter has collapsed into _____ aimed at everyone who ever approved the project.

tc-lampoon-1.explanation: Readers only complain when their own side is the target, so the cartoon must be mocking its subjects, which lampoon says; venerate and extol are praise.
tc-lampoon-1.stem: The weekly cartoon exists to _____ whoever happens to be in office, and its readers complain only when it turns on a politician they had voted for.

tc-levity-1.explanation: What the fine punishes is the joke, so the banned thing is humour, which levity names; decorum and deference are what the judge is insisting on instead.
tc-levity-1.stem: The judge allowed no _____ in her courtroom: a barrister who made a joke about the exhibit was fined before he had finished the sentence.

tc-mendacity-1.explanation: Set against honest error, a rehearsed and impossible account is deliberate lying, which mendacity names; probity, veracity and candor are all forms of honesty.
tc-mendacity-1.stem: What sank the testimony was not error but _____: the witness had rehearsed a version of the evening that could not possibly have happened.

tc-miscreant-1.explanation: The blank names whoever broke the windows and was caught for it, which is a miscreant; a pariah is merely shunned and the rest describe manner rather than wrongdoing.
tc-miscreant-1.stem: Every window along the terrace was broken that night, and the one _____ responsible was caught within a day by a doorbell camera nobody had noticed.

tc-nadir-1.explanation: Clients leaving and the founder going silent make March the worst moment, which nadir names; zenith, acme, apogee and pinnacle all point to the top instead.
tc-nadir-1.stem: March was the _____ of the whole affair: two clients left in a week, the lease ran out, and the founder stopped answering email altogether.

tc-occlude-1.explanation: The pumps run dry because nothing gets through, so the silt has blocked the pipes, which occlude means; inundate and saturate would fill them with water instead.
tc-occlude-1.stem: Silt carried down by the spring floods can _____ the intake pipes so completely that the pumps at the treatment works run dry before June.

tc-ossify-1.explanation: Temporary clauses left in place for sixty years harden into permanent ones, which ossify says; dissipate, fluctuate and erode would all have them fade or move.
tc-ossify-1.stem: A charter meant to be rewritten every decade has gone sixty years untouched, long enough for clauses adopted as temporary measures to _____ completely.

tc-pedestrian-1.explanation: A book cited rather than read, set against original research, has dull prose, which pedestrian names; lucid, meticulous and ebullient would all invite reading.
tc-pedestrian-1.stem: The research is genuinely original and the writing that carries it is _____, which is why the book is cited far more often than it is actually read.

tc-philistine-1.explanation: The insult lands on someone who would trade art for plumbing, which is what philistine means; a connoisseur is the opposite and the rest describe temperament.
tc-philistine-1.stem: Anyone who suggested selling two paintings to repair the roof was denounced as a _____, which ended the discussion without ever answering the question about the roof.

tc-polemical-1.explanation: Written to provoke a fight, and set against the hedged early work, the late papers are polemical; conciliatory, tentative and anodyne all avoid the argument.
tc-polemical-1.stem: Her early papers are careful and heavily hedged; the late ones are _____, written to provoke the field into a fight rather than to persuade it.

tc-predilection-1.explanation: She sought the difficult sources out and spent four years on them, so the blank is a liking, which predilection names; the other four are dislike or disregard.
tc-predilection-1.stem: Her _____ for difficult sources turned what was commissioned as a short article into four years of work in provincial archives nobody else had opened.

tc-proclivity-1.explanation: Bred to dig and doing it by instinct is a natural tendency, which proclivity names; aversion and apathy would mean the dog avoided or ignored the activity.
tc-proclivity-1.stem: The breed's _____ for digging is not a training failure but the thing it was bred to do, and no fence buried shallowly will survive a wet spring.

tc-propitious-1.explanation: Cheap money and a desperate landlord are conditions that favour the venture, which propitious names; precarious, arduous and untenable would all warn against it.
tc-propitious-1.stem: Cheap credit, an empty high street and a landlord desperate for any tenant at all made that spring unusually _____ for opening a shop.

tc-prosaic-1.explanation: An earlier train is an ordinary explanation, and disappointingly signals the letdown after elaborate theories, which is what prosaic captures; byzantine and arcane say the reverse.
tc-prosaic-1.stem: The disappearance invited every kind of theory for a fortnight, and the answer turned out to be disappointingly _____: she had taken an earlier train and told nobody.

tc-puerile-1.explanation: Grown politicians squabbling over who said a word first is childish, which puerile names; erudite, decorous and urbane would all describe the opposite behaviour.
tc-puerile-1.stem: The debate reached a point so _____ that two elected members spent a full minute arguing about which of them had used the word first.

tc-pugnacious-1.explanation: Four legal fights, one of them started from a hospital bed, describe someone eager to fight, which pugnacious names; phlegmatic, diffident and placid all say she would not.
tc-pugnacious-1.stem: Small, elderly and entirely _____, she had already sued three newspapers and was drafting a fourth complaint from her hospital bed.

tc-quixotic-1.explanation: A fine aim needing more money than the town could ever raise is idealistic and unworkable, which quixotic names; pragmatic, prudent and expedient all imply it could work.
tc-quixotic-1.stem: The plan to rebuild the pier by public subscription was _____ from the first meeting: the sum required was more than the town had raised in a century.

tc-rarefied-1.explanation: Forty buyers worldwide and no link to the ordinary economy make the market exclusive and remote, which rarefied names; volatile and nascent describe movement and youth instead.
tc-rarefied-1.stem: Prices in that _____ corner of the market answer to perhaps forty buyers worldwide and have not tracked the wider economy in thirty years.

tc-restive-1.explanation: Held in place with no explanation until the crew hid, the passengers are restless and impatient under restraint, which restive names; somnolent and placid say they settled.
tc-restive-1.stem: Kept on the tarmac for three hours with no explanation and no water, the passengers grew _____ enough that the crew stopped making announcements altogether.
